name: Crossby
summary: Terrace wine bar on Yangjae-cheon's café strip with live jazz sets and easy bistro plates.
description: Crossby sits along the Yangjae-cheon stream promenade, a quiet, leafy strip popular with Seocho locals rather than tourists. Inside it feels like a book-lined jazz lounge — warm lighting, a curated wine list, and a small stage for live jazz/live-band sets on select nights. The kitchen keeps it simple with pastas, risottos and a well-loved tteokbokki with seafood. Ask for the terrace on a mild evening and you can watch the stream path while you sip.
highlights: Live jazz/live-band nights (check Instagram for schedule)
Bacon tomato or myeongnan (pollock roe) rosé pasta
tips: Book via CatchTable, especially for evenings with live music — it fills up.
A short taxi or 13-min walk from Yangjae Station (Line 3/Sinbundang).
Weeknights are calmer for conversation; weekends lean lively.

reviews.text: Regulars describe it as cozy and classic, a favorite for dates and anniversaries, with live jazz performances a highlight.

name: Gwaenchana Sadang-iya
summary: Hand-carved Iberico ham sliced tableside at a warm, photogenic wine bar near Sadang.
description: Tucked into a quiet street on the Seocho/Sadang border, this wine bar built its name (a playful "it's okay, Sadang" pun) on Bellota-grade Iberico ham carved by hand at the table, paired with truffle-cream gnocchi and a well-chosen glass-pour wine list. The dining room is intimate and warmly lit with a private room available — good for a small group wanting a quieter conversation over wine rather than a loud bar scene.
tips: Ask staff for a wine recommendation — reviewers say every suggestion landed well.
No on-site parking; use nearby public lots.
About a 6-min walk from Sadang Station Exit 11 (Lines 2/4).

name: Terrace Wine & Restaurant
summary: Mediterranean-toned wine bar with a real terrace on the Yangjae-cheon café strip, open from lunch.
description: On the same leafy Yangjae-cheon promenade as several of the area's best wine bars, this two-storey spot leans into an "exotic," almost European terrace mood with wood beams, warm lamps and a proper outdoor seating area. It runs from lunch through late — useful if the family wants a relaxed daytime glass of wine with pasta rather than only a nightcap. The kitchen turns out pastas and a reliably good filet steak alongside a solid wine-by-the-glass list.

name: LP Bar Zeppelin
summary: A 30,000-record LP bar near Sinnonhyeon run by a DJ-owner of 28 years — take requests, sip a Guinness or highball.
description: Steps from Sinnonhyeon Station, Zeppelin is a proper LP bar: the owner is a 28-year veteran DJ who spins requests from a collection of roughly 30,000 vinyl records and music videos on a big screen. It skews toward an older, music-loving crowd — exactly the relaxed, nostalgic vibe that suits a 50-something couple who grew up on vinyl. Order the certified Guinness master-poured draft or a whisky highball, plus the melon-and-jamón plate, and settle in for a set.
highlights: Group seating for a party of 5
tips: It's more mainstream/crowd-pleasing than a hardcore audiophile bar — good for a first LP-bar experience.
Snack refills (the free rice-cracker starter) are famously generous.
A 3-min walk from Sinnonhyeon Station Exit 9.

reviews.text: Rated 4.3 from 321 Google reviews.

name: Highball Garden
summary: Izakaya-style highball specialist between Sinsa and Apgujeong — a different whisky-and-soda combo poured daily.

The bartenders rotate "today's highball" using a different whisky paired with soda or ginger ale, plus fruitier pisco, yuzu and wasabi riffs for the more adventurous. It's a relaxed, conversational bar — closer to a Tokyo izakaya than a loud cocktail club — and a good easy introduction to whisky highballs for guests who don't want a full cocktail menu.

name: Jangsaeng Health Center
summary: A former Korean herbal-tonic shop in Yeongdong Market reborn as a nostalgic, open-year-round cocktail bar.
description: Jangsaeng ("longevity") was once literally a geongangwon — a traditional Korean herbal tonic shop — inside Yeongdong Market near Nonhyeon Station, and the new owners kept the old apothecary bones while turning it into a cocktail bar. The concept plays on that history: a "naengmyeon cocktail" and other tongue-in-cheek riffs on Korean comfort food alongside proper cocktails, served in a warmly lit room with market-worn charm. It's open every day of the year, which makes it a reliable pick even around the Chuseok holiday.
highlights: Concept cocktails riffing on Korean comfort food
Braised pork belly (dongpa-yuk style) and kimchi
tips: Open 365 days a year — a safe bet if other bars close for Chuseok.
Sits inside old Yeongdong Market — half the fun is the walk in past shuttered market stalls at night.

summary: A modern, spacious bakery café near Apgujeong Rodeo famous for butter-rich croissants.
description: A modern, uncluttered bakery café off Apgujeong Rodeo, known locally for its butter-forward croissants and hand-drip coffee program. The room reads bright, open and design-forward, with reviewers noting a calm, modern mood good for a relaxed coffee break rather than a rushed takeaway.
tips: Closed on Chuseok day (25 Sep 2026) per venue notice.
A 6-min walk from Apgujeong Station Exit 1.
Croissants sell out by afternoon on busy days — go earlier.

name: Selected Nick's
summary: A sprawling multi-floor café steps from Gangnam Station, each level styled differently, with a rooftop terrace.
description: One of Gangnam's best-known large-format cafés, Selected Nick's occupies a basement-through-8th-floor building right outside Gangnam Station, with each level designed around a different theme — gallery-like art walls, a plant-filled floor, a rooftop terrace with skyline views. It's open late as a study/hangout café, and the tiramisu selection (several flavors) is the house signature. Easy for a group of 5 to spread out and find a table even at different times.
tips: Extremely central — literally at Gangnam Station Exit 4, easiest big-cafe stop after dinner.
Go up to the rooftop floor for the best view; lower floors get crowded.
Popular with students studying late — expect a lively, buzzy room.

name: Standard Bread Dosan
summary: A four-floor European-style bakery café near Dosan Park, famous for cream-brûlée French toast.
description: A big, design-forward bakery café spanning four floors near Dosan Park, with a European-bistro look — arched windows, warm wood, a real terrace. It's one of Apgujeong/Sinsa's most talked-about brunch-and-bakery stops, built for a leisurely brunch or afternoon coffee with room to spread out as a group.
tips: Very popular — go before noon on weekends to skip the wait.
A 6-min walk from Apgujeong Rodeo Station Exit 5.
Good for a relaxed family brunch before an afternoon in Apgujeong.

name: Cresstaun
summary: A calm, pet-friendly Apgujeong Rodeo bakery café known for its aeinspanner (whipped-cream cold brew).
description: A relaxed, softly lit bakery café near Apgujeong Rodeo Station with a loyal local following for its aeinspanner (whipped-cream-topped cold brew) and pastries. The interior stays quiet and unhurried, and it opens early, which makes it a good easy breakfast/coffee stop before a day out in Apgujeong.
tips: Opens at 7am — a good early coffee stop.

name: Hanip Bagel
summary: Bite-sized artisan bagels and a garden patio near Seoul Forest — a Seongsu bakery favorite.
description: A clean, bright bagel bakery near Seoul Forest known for its "one-bite" mini bagels in flavors like salt, jambon-beurre and honey cream cheese — an easy way to sample several flavors without committing to one full-size bagel. There's an outdoor garden patio, making it a pleasant stop for a light bite on the way to or from Seoul Forest park.
highlights: One-bite mini bagels (salt, jambon-beurre, honey cream cheese, corn cream cheese)
tips: A 5-min walk from Seoul Forest Station Exit 2.
Bagels are small — order a few flavors to share.

name: Maxim Plant
summary: A cavernous former Maxim coffee facility turned industrial-chic café in Hannam, with its own roastery and a terrace.
description: Maxim Plant is one of Seoul's best-known large-format cafés: a multi-level industrial space in Hannam built around Dongsuh/Maxim's coffee heritage, with exposed concrete, greenery, a working roastery and a rooftop terrace. It's huge — basement through three floors — so a family of 5 can always find a table, and the scale itself is part of the appeal.
tips: A 6-min walk from Hangangjin Station Exit 3.
Huge and popular — arrive off-peak (weekday morning) for easier seating.
